subject.title: [Bug]: exec spawn UNKNOWN after gateway restart — child_process pool not rebuilt

question: Should maintainers require native Windows current-main reproduction before any repair work on this post-restart `spawn UNKNOWN` report?
rationale: The reported user impact is serious, but current source contradicts the proposed pool root cause and related issues do not prove this exact symptom, so automation cannot safely choose a code fix yet.

options.title: Require Windows Repro First
options.body: Collect a native Windows current-main run with a restart-required `config.patch`, immediate exec command, logs, and process details before opening or queueing a fix.

options.title: Open Narrow Hardening Follow-Up
options.body: Split transient Windows `UNKNOWN` spawn retry hardening into a separate issue only if maintainers accept the risk of fixing without proving the restart trigger.

options.title: Close After Negative Repro
options.body: If a native Windows current-main run cannot reproduce the symptom, close this report as no longer reproducible and ask for a fresh issue with logs.

recommendation.title: Require Windows Repro First
recommendation.body: Collect a native Windows current-main run with a restart-required `config.patch`, immediate exec command, logs, and process details before opening or queueing a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history link is exec spawn fallback and Windows exec invocation ownership, which are the likely first code surfaces to inspect after proof arrives.
